objective: Audit recent activation history and frontier decisions to determine whether explicit highest-value focused-task selection produces better information flow.
bottleneck: Prior activations had durable conclusions but task choice was opportunistic from a queue.
question: Does the current focused-task selector improve learning efficiency relative to the repository's prior opportunistic task choice?
action: Audited durable evidence only: (1) read state/LEARNING_STATE.md in full, including the Active strategy delta (Gap / Strategy Delta / Expected Effect / Observed Effect / Decision / Next), the 17-row research frontier table, and the 15-row recent learning history table; (2) read state/STATE.md through line 851, covering the pre-frontier infrastructure activations (2026-10-02..2026-10-04) and the frontier-era activations (37263008074, 37304873966, 37314710995, 37318950814, 37361000967, 37394344201, 37414038601); (3) read the controller selector implementation .github/scripts/campaign_controller.py (task_rank, candidate_tasks_for_role, select_task, render_prompt) and .github/scripts/evaluate_research_process.py + synthesize_campaign.py to establish how selection and its observation are actually recorded; (4) read state/campaign/current_task.json, state/campaign/task_queue.json, state/campaign/runs/44934332878/campaign_status.json, task_queue_initial.json and agent_01_contract.json; (5) read logs/ACTIVATION-2026-10-02..2026-10-06.md section headers plus the per-activation selection-basis lines. Classified each post-contract activation for durable outcome and for selection path. No experiment was run and no process artifact was changed; the audit was designed so its own conclusion cannot be helped by any edit.
verified: READ-VERIFIED (repo-native read of state/LEARNING_STATE.md lines 7-13, 42-59): the learning layer itself records the counter-factual baseline in durable form: activation 37260572520 (2026-10-05) states 'the objective came from the queued receipt item rather than a frontier cell', and activation 37261348530 records a frontier-first selection whose execution was blocked, producing a PENDING EXECUTION cell with no verdict. Two activations therefore document the opportunistic/queued path with a measured outcome.

READ-VERIFIED (state/LEARNING_STATE.md frontier table, lines 27-35): four of the five cells the contract cites as closed are each present exactly once with a terminal verdict and no re-test row: mean-reversion FALSIFIED (:27, 37263008074), cross-sectional relative strength FALSIFIED (:28, 37304873966), volatility targeting FALSIFIED (:29, 37314710995), 20-day breakout continuation FALSIFIED (:35, 37414038601). The momentum cell is NOT a single clean row: :30 is a one-cell row containing only the cell label, :31 (longer-horizon momentum) is physically inserted between :30 and :32, and the momentum status/evidence content sits at :32 with no leading pipe and only three cells. The table is malformed at that point, so the momentum cell's identity is split across two rows even though its verdict text appears once.

READ-VERIFIED (state/LEARNING_STATE.md learning history rows 53-59): the same five cells are recorded as decisively closed, each with an independent-verification MATCH or 3-gate MATCH and a determinism assertion, and with no equivalent re-test recorded against any of them. Rows :50 (37257258857) and :51 (37260572520) are two terminal rows for the SAME falsification (regime-adaptive MA), with :50 explicitly deferring to :51 ('falsified (see 37260572520)'). The five-cell framing also omits :31 (longer-horizon momentum, 37394344201) and :34 (cross-sectional momentum), and the file's own text claims six closures (:58 'a fifth time', :59 'a sixth time').

READ-VERIFIED (.github/scripts/campaign_controller.py lines 198-225): selector comparison is purely ordinal (benefit_order HIGH/MEDIUM/LOW over expected_information_gain, downstream_leverage, falsification_power, verifiability; cost_order over effort, complexity, execution_risk; task_id tiebreak) with no numeric score; lines 269-383 bind the selected task to an immutable contract; lines 386-415 render the role guidance and the single-question firewall into every fresh session.

READ-VERIFIED (state/campaign/current_task.json + task_queue.json): the authoritative task_queue.json remains unmodified with P-001 status OPEN and selected_agent 1; R-004 is already status RESOLVED. Selection metadata in campaign_status.json (selection_history[0].compared_against = [P-001,P-002,P-004,P-003,P-006]) is consistent with the contract.
unverified: SELECTION MECHANISM (NOT MEASURED): this campaign selects work by controller-side ordinal ranking inside campaign_controller.py, whereas every cited historical cell records selection by a worker judgement of the frontier table (logs/ACTIVATION-2026-10-06.md line 9: 'Selection basis: frontier-first'). The selector actually evaluated here is therefore not the mechanism that produced the five cited closures. No durable evidence links the controller selector's decisions to learning efficiency.

NO BASELINE MEASUREMENT: no durable document records experiments-per-decision or duplicate-experiment counts for the pre-contract era, so no rate comparison between opportunistic and frontier-first choice is computable from durable state. CORRECTED BY INDEPENDENT REVIEW: the stronger clause 'no per-activation information-gain classification exists' was FALSE as written. The Information Gain column of the learning-history table (state/LEARNING_STATE.md:44, :46, :50, :52) DOES classify the opportunistic-era activations (e.g. :44 'Framework capability established'; :46 'Methodology gap closed'; :50 'One MA-crossover rescue hypothesis eliminated with two independent paths'). It is retrospective and authored alongside the contract (logs/ACTIVATION-2026-10-05.md:293-308) and has no denominators, so it does not rescue a rate comparison, but it is real evidence that the earlier clause wrongly denied. Durable wasted-work records also exist and cut both ways: logs/ACTIVATION-2026-10-02.md:233-240 and state/STATE.md:487-489 (non-reproducible prior figures, 9/45 tests failing), logs/ACTIVATION-2026-10-04.md:705-707, :736-738, :762-799 (execution blocked; 8/10 tests failing on first run), versus frontier-era rework at logs/ACTIVATION-2026-10-05.md:540-548 (three check defects + one verifier defect), :618 (one verifier defect) and state/STATE.md:633-658 (four CSRS defects). Because rework is recorded in BOTH eras, wasted work cannot be pointed in either direction, which reinforces rather than weakens the no-comparison conclusion.

SCOPE CONFOUND: the frontier-first era added the a-priori falsification prediction, the independent verifier gate, determinism assertion, and manifest/preflight/leakage gates per activation (e.g. logs/ACTIVATION-2026-10-05.md lines 680-697; logs/ACTIVATION-2026-10-06.md lines 11, 50). The 'no equivalent re-tests' observation cannot be attributed to selection policy alone because evidence standards changed at the same boundary.

OBSERVATION IS SELF-REPORT: task_selection_observation in agent records is authored by the agent, not derived from evidence (evaluate_research_process.py lines 47-55 read the field verbatim; synthesize_campaign.py line 181 copies it verbatim). It cannot serve as an independent efficiency measurement without a cross-check that does not exist in the controller.

COMMAND-LEVEL BLOCKER: the bash tool is denied at this layer for every invocation (project permission rule). No script was executed, so no recomputation, regression run, or controller dry-run was performed for this audit; every finding above rests on direct repository-native reads. This is an execution-environment signal, not a research finding.

TIMESTAMP PRECISION: only the environment message time 2026-11-21T18:14:33Z and the before-capture time 2026-11-21T18:14:29Z (state/campaign/runs/44934332878/agents/agent_01_before.json) were observed; no wall-clock read succeeded, so no per-step UTC timestamps exist for this activation.
observed_effect: Choosing this task produced a bounded, decision-relevant audit result with zero code change and zero regression risk. It did not produce the comparison the task asks for: the controller-side ordinal selector that exists today is not the mechanism that produced the cited frontier closures, and no durable record supports a rate comparison against the opportunistic era. Two genuine process observations beyond the contract's question: this is the first activation in the series to test the selector itself rather than exercise it, and its deliverable is a narrowing of the prior RETAIN rather than another demonstration. An independent read-only falsification review of this audit found two of its own supporting clauses over-stated (no-information-gain-classification; no duplicate terminal rows) and both were corrected here rather than suppressed; the review also surfaced two previously unrecorded defects in state/LEARNING_STATE.md itself (:30-32 malformed momentum row; :50-:51 duplicated regime-adaptive MA terminal row).
uncertainty_targeted: Whether explicit highest-value focused-task selection measurably improves learning efficiency relative to the repository's prior opportunistic task choice.
uncertainty_reduced: Reduces uncertainty about the justification for the prior RETAIN: the five-cell evidence is real and durable (no duplicate terminal rows, each cell independently verified), but the controller selector is not the mechanism that produced it and no pre-contract rate baseline exists, so 'selector improves efficiency' is unmeasured rather than supported. Converts an apparently verified process claim into an explicitly unresolved one and names the three observations that would settle it (duplicate-terminal-row scan, per-activation information-gain classification, odd/even task_selection_observation trend). Uncertainty about whether any selector change would help is unchanged and is not claimed as reduced.
research_result: No research experiment was run; this activation produced no market, dataset, or hypothesis evidence and makes no quantitative claim about any asset. All quantitative figures cited above are read from pre-existing durable artifacts and were not recomputed (bash denied). Process finding (two layers, deliberately separated): (a) RETAINED as the operating rule - explicit frontier-first / ordinal qualitative selection is auditable, produced six decisively-closed signal-class cells each with an independent-verification MATCH and a determinism assertion, and has a measured negative control (37260572520 queued-objective selection, with the blocked follow-on cell at 37261348530). Correctness caveat on that count: the six closures span two mechanisms, not one - four under worker frontier judgement (mean-reversion 37263008074, CSRS 37304873966, volatility targeting 37314710995, momentum 37318950814) and two whose provenance is mixed or queue-sourced (breakout 37414038601, logged as 'task R-004' from the campaign queue; cross-sectional momentum). Only the first four are clean evidence for frontier selection as an operating rule. (b) REJECTED - the stronger claim that this selector improves learning efficiency RELATIVE TO OPPORTUNISTIC CHOICE. The cited evidence does not support it: the controller-side ordinal selector that exists today is not the mechanism that produced those closures, no durable pre-contract baseline records duplicate-experiment counts, and the one per-activation information-gain classification that does exist is retrospective and has no denominators. This supersedes the prior 'RETAIN (verified)' framing in state/LEARNING_STATE.md line 12, which attributed the outcome to selection; that framing is contradicted by the same file's own 37260572520/37261348530 rows. The contradiction is recorded, not erased, and no history was rewritten. TWO DEFECTS IN THE DURABLE RECORD ITSELF, found by an independent read-only falsification review of this audit and confirmed by direct re-read: (i) state/LEARNING_STATE.md:30-32 is a malformed frontier row - the momentum cell label sits alone at :30, the longer-horizon row is inserted at :31, and the momentum status/evidence content at :32 has no leading pipe and only three cells, so the row cannot be parsed as a table row; (ii) :50 and :51 are two terminal rows for the same regime-adaptive MA falsification. These are reported as observed defects; repairing them is out of scope for this activation (the contract's scope is a bounded process judgment) and is handed off rather than performed.

candidate_tasks.primary_question: Does the frontier table's 'Next bounded action' field predict the next activation's selected task often enough to justify treating the frontier as the primary selector rather than a record?
candidate_tasks.bottleneck: The frontier table records verdicts well but its Next column has repeatedly pointed at work that a later activation did not select, so the frontier may be a history log rather than a live selection surface.
candidate_tasks.objective: For each of the last six activations, compare the frontier's recorded Next action against the task actually executed and classify the pair as followed / superseded / ignored.
candidate_tasks.scope: Use state/LEARNING_STATE.md frontier rows, learning-history rows, logs/ACTIVATION-2026-10-05.md and logs/ACTIVATION-2026-10-06.md only; no experiments.
candidate_tasks.out_of_scope: Do not rerun experiments, do not modify the frontier schema, and do not redesign the controller.
candidate_tasks.deliverable: A six-row table of predicted-vs-executed task pairs plus one bounded process judgment.
candidate_tasks.success_criterion: The predictive value of the frontier Next field is classified as supported, unsupported, or unverified with cited line references.
candidate_tasks.stop_condition: Stop once the six pairs are tabulated or the durable record is shown to be insufficient to tabulate them.
candidate_tasks.verification_requirement: Controller-side validation plus re-reading each cited frontier row and log section.
candidate_tasks.evidence_basis: CONFIRMED DEFECTS from this audit's independent review: state/LEARNING_STATE.md:30 is a one-cell momentum label row, :31 (longer-horizon momentum) is inserted before it resolves, and :32 carries the momentum status/evidence with no leading pipe and only three cells; :50 (37257258857) and :51 (37260572520) are two terminal rows for the same regime-adaptive MA falsification, with :50 deferring to :51.

candidate_tasks.primary_question: Does the task queue's qualitative priority ordering select genuinely different work at successive campaign slots or repeatedly the same class of work?
candidate_tasks.bottleneck: Ordinal task_rank ordering plus role filtering may collapse several HIGH-priority tasks onto the same class of work, leaving distinct high-value cells unselected across a campaign.
candidate_tasks.objective: Inspect the campaign selection history and the OPEN queue and determine whether the ordering diversifies or concentrates the selected work.
candidate_tasks.scope: Use state/campaign/task_queue.json, campaign_status.json selection_history, and the controller task_rank ordering in .github/scripts/campaign_controller.py:198-225 only; no experiments, no scoring redesign, no .github/scripts/ edits.
candidate_tasks.out_of_scope: Do not introduce a numeric reward score, do not rerun experiments, and do not modify .github/scripts/.
candidate_tasks.deliverable: A bounded selection-diversity assessment over the OPEN queue.
candidate_tasks.success_criterion: Selection behavior is classified as diversifying, concentrating, or unverified using the durable queue and selection history.
candidate_tasks.stop_condition: Stop once the queue ordering and selection history have been compared for all OPEN tasks.
candidate_tasks.verification_requirement: Controller-side validation of the record and re-inspection of task_rank ordering inputs.
candidate_tasks.evidence_basis: This audit found the breakout cell's provenance is mixed in a way that weakens any clean frontier-vs-queue dichotomy: logs/ACTIVATION-2026-10-06.md:7 labels it 'Objective (task R-004)' and state/activation_status.json:9 says 'Execute task R-004 from the campaign queue', matching state/campaign/task_queue.json:213-235 verbatim, while the same log line 9 states 'Selection basis: frontier-first'.
